card.stem: The sketch shows a portion of the external wall and the first floor of a two storey dwelling house. The external wall is a 350 mm concrete block wall. The cavity is filled with blown polystyrene beads. The first floor is a floating tongued and grooved hardwood floor, on 20 mm plywood, on 225 mm × 40 mm joists with a plasterboard ceiling beneath.
card.questionText: To a scale of 1:5, draw a vertical section through the external wall and the first floor. The section should show the typical construction details from a level 300 mm below the plasterboard ceiling, through the wall, joists and floor, to a level 400 mm above the finished floor. Include four typical dimensions on your drawing. Show 1.0 metre width of floor.

rows.contextNote: Any 9 of the above details ( 4 marks each). Credit the best NINE acceptable details at 4 marks each, capped at 36. Marked details: external render 19 mm; external leaf solid block 100 mm; 150 mm full-fill cavity insulation; cavity ties; internal leaf solid block 100 mm; internal plaster 15 mm; skirting board; floating tongued and grooved hardwood floor; acoustic or adhesive layer for fixing the floor boards; plywood deck 20 mm; adhesive tape to the wall and plywood; floor joists 225 × 40 mm; plasterboard taped to the wall and plaster skim.

options: Floating tongued and grooved hardwood floor
Acoustic layer or adhesive layer for fixing floor boards
Adhesive tape to wall and plywood

rows.contextNote: Four appropriate typical dimensions on the section, 1 each.

card.stem: The sketch shows a single storey extension to a dwelling house. The external wall of the extension is a single leaf, 215 mm solid concrete block wall. The wall has an external render but it is not insulated. It is proposed to improve the insulation properties of the external wall of the extension by fixing insulation, 200 mm in thickness, to the outside of the wall.
card.questionText: Using notes and freehand sketches show one method of fixing the insulation to the solid block wall of the extension. Specify the insulation material to be used.

rows.contextNote: Such as: a stainless steel base track fixed to the wall at DPC level carries the first row of boards; the boards are fixed with a special adhesive.
A second, different step. Such as: the next rows fixed in a staggered pattern; mechanical fixings, typically seven per square metre, drilled through the insulation into the wall and hammered home.
Such as: polystyrene; mineral fibre board; phenolic foam.
Quality of the sketches: excellent 8, good 6, fair 4.

card.questionText: A modern wood burning stove, as shown in the sketch, is fitted with a back boiler. The back boiler is connected to an indirect cylinder to provide hot water for a dwelling house. Using a single-line labelled diagram, show the pipework necessary to supply hot water to the kitchen sink. Include the following on your diagram: water storage tank and overflow pipe; rising main; stove and back boiler; hot water cylinder and pipework; location of all necessary valves. On your diagram, show the insulation to the water storage tank and to all the pipework.

rows.contextNote: Any 9 of the above details (4 marks each). Credit the best NINE acceptable details at 4 marks each, capped at 36. Secondary circulation: rising main; cold water storage tank and ball valve; overflow; cold feed from storage to the indirect cylinder; indirect hot water cylinder; expansion pipe from the cylinder; supply to the sink. Primary circulation: supply to the expansion tank; expansion tank and ball valve; overflow; cold water feed and primary return; wood burning stove and back boiler; expansion pipe and primary flow; valves; insulation to the storage tank and pipework; labelling.

options: Cold water storage tank and ball valve
Cold feed from storage to indirect hot water cylinder
Cold water feed and primary return
Insulation to water storage tank and pipework

rows.contextNote: Quality of the sketch: excellent 8, good 6, fair 4.

card.stem: A non load-bearing timber stud partition, with plasterboard on both sides, separates a kitchen and living room, as shown in the sketch.
card.questionText: Using notes and freehand sketches, show the steps involved in applying a plaster skim finish to one side of the stud partition.

rows.contextNote: Such as: sheeting over the floor; the joints taped and the partition sealed to the walls and ceiling; plaster added to water in a clean bucket and mixed free of lumps.

card.questionText: Explain, with the aid of notes and freehand sketches, any five of the following: strip foundation; housing joint; laser beam; thermostatic valve; collar tie; radon sump; roof-light window; smart meter; external ramp.

rows.contextNote: Explain any five of the nine terms. Each term is marked separately: primary communication of relevant information 6 and other communication 4, in notes or sketches (the scheme reserves no fixed split between them). Strip Foundation: a simple, common and economical concrete foundation, reinforced with steel bars, supporting a solid or cavity wall centrally; typically three times the wall thickness wide and as thick as the wall; the load spreads at 45 degrees to the ground. Housing joint: a basic joint joining two pieces at right angles: a trench removed from one piece takes the other, glued for strength; used in cabinets, bookcases and shelving; simple, strong and easy to make. Laser beam: a light beam used in printers, cutting and welding and barcode scanning; on site a laser projector sends out the beam and a staff with an adjustable sensor detects it, giving levels at different points on the site or on internal walls. Thermostatic Valve: a valve fitted to a radiator in a central heating system, controlling its heat output to give the desired room temperature; inexpensive, it reduces heating costs and CO₂ emissions. Collar tie: a member in tension stretching from rafter to rafter, tying them into a triangle for structural stability; purlins may rest on it; typically 200 × 50 mm; it may form the ceiling in an attic conversion. Radon sump: a compartment placed centrally in the hardcore under the ground floor to collect radon gas through gaps in its walls; pipes from its connectors carry the gas outside the building, where it dissipates. Roof-light window: a window fitted in a sloping roof (or a special roof light for a flat roof), letting light and ventilation into an attic; double or triple glazed and highly insulated, fitting neatly into the roof surface; top or pivot hung. Smart meter: records the electricity used in the home and shows its cost at any time, giving the householder control; may be topped up with credit; can also record gas or water. External ramp: a sloping path for easy access for people with restricted mobility, wheelchairs and buggies: gradient 1:20, sections no longer than 9.0 m, at least 1200 mm clear width, non-slip, lit from the sides.
